jobs.description:
**Job Description**: Develop sim2real reinforcement learning (RL) training pipelines for humanoid robots. Train and test robot policies via reinforcement learning for in-home humanoid robots. Optimize training pipelines for improved performance and training speed. Modeling of physical systems (including robot dynamics, sensor modeling, contact parameter tuning) to close the gap between simulation and physical systems. Collecting, cleaning and retargeting human motion data for use in RL training pipelines. Supporting the test and debug of RL policies in simulation and on physical hardware.  
  
**Requirements**: Master’s degree or foreign degree equivalent in Robotics, AI/Machine Learning, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field and one (1) year of experience in a Robotics & Machine Learning occupation or related in the job offered.  
  
**Skills:**  
  
Experience and/or education must include:

* Rigid body dynamics and/or dynamical systems for training, deploying and testing reinforcement learned policies for humanoid robots.
* Implement production-grade Python code for reinforcement learning (RL) and other machine learning training pipelines.
* Reinforcement learned algorithms, techniques, and sim2real approaches as they pertain to robotics to perform various human-like capabilities, including whole-body loco-manipulation.
* Implement and debug real-time software in C++ deployed on robots to satisfy various real-time constraints.
* Model physical systems, including multi-body hybrid dynamic systems with contact, in a simulated environment to identify gaps between simulation and hardware and the ability to understand how to accurately model the hardware in simulation.
* Root-cause analysis as it pertains to robotic systems and the ability to quickly troubleshoot issues.
* Forward and inverse kinematics as they pertain to humanoid system training using human motion data.

Compensation Range: $130,146 - $300,000

**ABOUT MINERVA**

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.

**THE ROLE**
------------

A warehouse full of consumer data does nothing for a marketer until they can sort, filter and chart it in the time it takes to ask the question.

Our data team builds the consumer graph and each brand's first-party models, and our data scientists train scores on top. This seat makes all of it usable in the product: first-party fields that respond instantly, scores on the pages marketers already use, segments that stay current, and an agent that turns a plain-English question into the right query against a brand's own data.

This is an IC or senior IC seat on product engineering, working day to day with data engineering and data science. Your counterpart on the warehouse side is our Staff Data Engineer, who owns the golden model and publishes the semantic views you build on.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

* **Own how first-party data performs in the app.** Any field a brand connects can be sorted, filtered and charted without a live warehouse query. You decide what gets precomputed, where it lives and how it stays fresh.
* **Own how our models reach marketers.** Propensity, LTV, churn and product-fit scores on the person, segment and product pages, with full distributions instead of a single number.
* **Own dynamic segments.** Segments that update as new data lands, with stats ready for activation.
* **Own the in-app agent's query tool,** built on the semantic views our data platform team publishes. You own the path from a marketer's question to the right rows.
* **Own the product side of the sync.** What gets precomputed, and the path from Postgres to the synced client. Each hop costs money and time, and you choose on purpose.
* **Extend the pipelines.** You mostly build on what the data team produces. When a feature needs a table that doesn't exist, you write the model or pipeline step yourself.
* **Ship end to end.** One feature can mean a Python Lambda, a Zero schema change and a TanStack Start page. You ship all three.

**OUR STACK**
-------------

* **App:** TypeScript, TanStack Start, React 19, Tailwind and Base UI, on Vite and Bun.
* **Sync:** Zero on Postgres, schema in Drizzle. The app reads from a live-synced local copy of the data instead of request-response endpoints.
* **AI:** Mastra for agents, Temporal for long-running work.
* **Backend:** Python on AWS Lambda.
* **Data:** Snowflake, including semantic views and Cortex.

**WHAT YOU HAVE**
-----------------

* Production experience with a cloud data warehouse. Snowflake preferred.
* Production TypeScript, and backend services shipped on AWS: Lambda or similar.
* You're current. You know what shipped in AI tooling this month and what changed in the latest release of the packages you depend on.
* You build things on your own time, and you can show us.
* You're in New York City or willing to relocate.

**YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU ARE…**
----------------------------------

* A **full-stack engineer at a data-heavy SaaS company** who ended up owning the warehouse because someone had to, and liked it.
* A **product engineer at a warehouse-native analytics or activation company** who has spent years making Snowflake feel fast inside an app.
* A **backend engineer who has shipped on a sync engine** like Zero, Replicache or ElectricSQL, and wants a dataset big enough to stress it. We'd be especially impressed by this one.
* A **data engineer tired of handing tables to other teams** who wants to own the feature the table ends up in.
* Or you don't fit any of these neatly, but you built something this year that changed how you think data should reach a user. Apply.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**
---------------------------

* **First 90 days:** new scores and first-party tables reach the app through a repeatable system you built.
* **First 6 months:** any first-party field can be sorted, filtered and charted without a live warehouse query, and the in-app agent's query tool runs on your layer.

**COMPENSATION**

$170,000–$236,000 base salary, depending on level. Meaningful equity. Medical, dental and vision.

**HOW TO APPLY**
----------------

Skip the cover letter. The application asks for a demo of something you built that's relevant to what we do at Minerva: a link, a repo or a two-minute video. Applications without a demo won't be reviewed.

**WHERE WE WORK**

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

Every full-time role includes equity; medical, dental and vision coverage; unlimited PTO; a monthly fitness stipend; and an annual company offsite. We'd rather pay people well than buy perks nobody uses.

**Explore our work**  
Captions — Our flagship creative workspace
  
Tesseract — Our professional video engine for AI agents
  
Research — The foundation models we build in-house
  
Updates — The latest from Mirage
  
TechCrunch, Forbes, Fast Company — Press  
  
**Our Investors**

We’re very fortunate to have some the best investors and entrepreneurs backing us, including **Index Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz,** **General Catalyst**, Uncommon Projects, Kevin Systrom, Mike Krieger, Lenny Rachitsky, Antoine Martin, Julie Zhuo, Ben Rubin, Jaren Glover, SVAngel, 20VC, Ludlow Ventures, Chapter One, and more.

*Please note that most of our roles will require you to be in-person at our NYC HQ (located in Union Square)*

**About the role**

We want Tesseract to render 3D that is indistinguishable from footage. You'll be the founding engineer for photoreal 3D in Tesseract, our Rust-based, cross-platform graphics and media rendering engine.

Tesseract already renders video, motion graphics, effects and compositing in a color- managed pipeline. You'll build 3D to the same standard: a fast interactive preview for editing, and a physically based final render, path-traced or hybrid ray-traced, that produces film-quality frames for export. Both run from one scene, material and lighting model, so what people see while they edit is what they export.

Scenes are authored by people and by AI agents, so render cost, failure modes and APIs matter as much as image quality. This is a foundational role: you'll make the core architectural decisions and help build the team around them.

**What you'll do**

* Define the architecture for photoreal 3D: how ray tracing, rasterization and denoising divide the work, and how that maps onto Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D and WebGPU.
* Build light transport: global illumination, reflections and refraction, soft shadows from area lights, and volumetrics such as haze, fog and light shafts.
* Build a physically based model for materials, lights and cameras: energy-conserving materials (metal, glass, clearcoat, sheen, translucency), lights in real-world units, and a camera with exposure, depth of field and motion blur.
* Own image quality: sampling, antialiasing, accumulation, denoising and firefly suppression, with frames that stay stable and deterministic across a video export.
* Scale scenes to production complexity with acceleration structures, instancing, culling and memory management, for millions of triangles and tens of thousands of objects.
* Integrate 3D into Tesseract's video, motion graphics and compositing pipeline, including ACES color management and render passes such as depth, normals, motion vectors and light groups.
* Make render cost predictable and rendering robust: performance budgets, profiling, and headless batch rendering on local and cloud GPUs.
* Design 3D APIs that work for people and AI agents alike: a clear scene representation, actionable validation errors, fast previews and render cost known before the render.
* Work with engine, product and AI teams, and help hire and grow the 3D rendering team.

**What makes you a great fit**

* Deep experience building physically based renderers in production: film or offline renderers, path tracers, or game engines with ray-traced or hybrid lighting.
* Strong command of light transport: the rendering equation, Monte Carlo integration, importance sampling, material models and denoising.
* Hands-on GPU ray tracing: building and traversing acceleration structures (BVHs), hardware ray-tracing APIs such as Metal ray tracing, Vulkan ray tracing or DXR, and compute-based fallbacks.
* A solid understanding of modern rasterization pipelines, and of how hybrid renderers combine rasterization with ray tracing.
* Hands-on experience with Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D or WebGPU, including compute shaders, GPU profiling and GPU debugging.
* Proficiency in Rust or C++, with strong reasoning about memory, concurrency and performance.
* Strong foundations in the mathematics of graphics: linear algebra, geometry, probability and sampling.
* An eye for realism: you can look at a frame, say why it doesn't read as real, and fix the cause.
* Experience owning complex technical projects and making architectural decisions in ambiguous problem spaces.

**Even better if…**

* You've worked on the internals of a production renderer or engine such as Cycles, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray, Karma, Unreal Engine (Lumen or its path tracer) or Unity HDRP.
* You've built or integrated ML denoisers, or worked on neural rendering.
* You've worked with color management (ACES, OpenColorIO), HDR output or film-look pipelines.
* You've built on cross-platform graphics abstractions such as wgpu, including extending them where they lack features such as ray tracing.
* You've optimized rendering for Apple silicon or mobile GPUs.
* You have experience with Rust, video compositing, or integrating 2D and 3D rendering in creative tools.

**Senior Backend Platform Engineer, MyLawAdmin (Node, TypeScript, Postgres)**

Over the past year we built a multi-tenant practice-management platform that runs law firms day to day operations. It includes a staff dashboard, a client portal, an admin console and the backend behind all of them. We are hiring a Senior Backend Platform Engineer to own how that platform runs and help ship and maintain the core and feature service offerings.

You will work directly with the law firm principal who designed and built the system, who leads the platform and its architecture, and with a senior developer who works firm-side and ships feature lanes end to end. Product ideas come from the two of them; your job is to understand how everything works and runs, say where it should run differently, and ship the code. The codebase is a year old, test-heavy, and documented with numbered architecture decision records.

What you will do:

* Learn how the whole platform runs, service by service, and become the person who can answer where anything happens and why.
* Own the unattended layer: the services, workers, scheduled jobs, queues and integrations that run without anyone clicking.
* Own the data layer in production: schema changes, migrations and backfills with rollbacks, and tenant isolation that holds up under review.
* Own reliability and security: observability, incident response, secrets and access, and getting us ready for an outside review.
* Answer feature briefs from the principal and the senior developer with a contract they can build against, then build your half.
* Ship every week in small reviewed pull requests, and write the short design note before the code when a change deserves one.

Tech stack:

* Backend: Fastify 5, TypeScript, Node 22, Zod, pino, Sentry.
* Data: Postgres with hand-written SQL migrations and row-level security; Redis for leases and queues; SpiceDB for authorization
* Frontends you will wire into: Next.js 15 and 16, React 19, our own design system.
* Tooling: GitHub Actions on self-hosted runners, Vitest against a real Postgres, an OSV supply-chain gate.

What we are looking for:

* Experience building and running backend services in Node and TypeScript, including at least one multi-tenant SaaS you kept in production
* You read an unfamiliar codebase quickly and find the running path: where a request enters, which worker picks it up, where it is logged
* Strong Postgres: you write SQL and migrations by hand, you have run a backfill on a live table with a rollback ready, you have used row-level security or another tenant-isolation model, and you can read a query plan
* You have built or operated a queue or outbox: idempotency, retries with backoff, dead letters, at-least-once delivery
* You instrument what you ship, and you have been the person paged for it
* Security habits: secrets, sessions and tokens, rate limiting, audit logs; you can write a threat model for a change
* You write integration tests against a real database as part of every change, and short design notes and PR descriptions a colleague can act on

Nice to have:

* Transactional email or SMS at volume: webhooks, bounces, suppression lists
* Authorization systems such as SpiceDB or OpenFGA
* Legal-tech, compliance or regulated-data experience
* Enough React to connect a backend door to an existing screen; no design work is expected

Why join us:

* You own how the platform runs, not tickets, and ship to real users every week
* A test-heavy, documented codebase with real multi-tenant and security problems to solve
* Direct collaboration with the principal and one senior developer
* Flexible hybrid schedule in Brooklyn
